title: Founder Signal — Series-A Conviction Hero
description: A stripped-back hero engineered for the first impression that precedes a $10M ask — one display-scale positioning sentence, a centered product mockup, and a discreet raise-metadata line that answers 'how much and who' without stealing focus from the thesis.
philosophy: This template exists to plant a single, unforgettable conviction in the room before the next slide loads. It refuses to fragment attention with subheads, bullet arrays, or decorative flourishes that dilute a founder's clearest thought. The aggressive type scale treats the positioning sentence as the product itself, making it feel self-evident rather than sold. Deep navy and off-white stay inside the visual language institutional investors already trust, so the idea — not the deck — commands the room.
goodFor: Series-A and Series-B fundraising opener slides
Single-sentence positioning statements that must land in under three seconds
Product-led narratives where a hero mockup image carries the proof
VC partner meetings where the first impression anchors everything that follows
avoidFor: Chart-heavy quarterly business reviews requiring data density
Multi-feature product comparisons or competitive landscape grids
Decks requiring warm, playful, or high-saturation visual tone
Slides that must carry three or more distinct content blocks simultaneously
author: harness

examples.promptCore: The slide should feel like a conviction statement delivered in a silent boardroom — institutional restraint where every absent element is a deliberate choice. Cathedral-like vertical symmetry lets the display sentence occupy the room as a self-evident truth rather than a claim being argued. The product mockup serves as visual proof anchored below, its presence grounding the abstract without fighting for dominance in the hierarchy. Avoid any decorative texture, gradient noise, border accents, or illustrative flourishes; the atmosphere of quiet confidence must come entirely from proportion and negative space.

examples.layoutNotes: 12-column grid with a 10% outer margin on all sides; the display-scale positioning sentence spans columns 2–11, centered vertically in the upper-third zone to command the eye on entry. A product mockup image is anchored at true vertical center, slightly oversized so it bleeds below the type band and implies depth without a card or container. The raise-metadata line — amount and lead investor — sits right-aligned at the bottom margin, typeset at the smallest readable size so it answers the room's silent question without competing. No header band, no logo row; the positioning sentence inherits the logo's structural authority.

examples.promptCore: The slide carries the composed authority of a partner-meeting whiteboard — one dominant claim commands the eye before supporting evidence earns its place below a subtle dividing line. Compositional rhythm is top-weighted and sparse, letting whitespace function as confidence rather than emptiness. The mood is institutional restraint meeting founder conviction: nothing decorative, nothing parenthetical, every element load-bearing. Avoid gradient overlays, icon clusters, or any visual texture that disrupts the clean typographic plane.

examples.layoutNotes: 12-column grid; primary content block anchors to cols 2–11 with a generous outer margin creating deliberate breathing room on both sides. A single dominant callout — one outsized stat or conviction phrase — occupies the upper vertical third, separated from two or three subordinate support points by a full-width hairline rule. The support tier uses equal-width columns below the rule, each holding a compact label-value pair or a single declarative clause. Slide index appears bottom-right; no header band, no decorative borders or background fill.
